## The model: recall is scope-key fan-out, not a workspace filter

`memory_canonical` is one row per fact `(id, payload jsonb, …, state)`. There is **no
workspace column in the recall path** — the store recalls by an opaque **scope key** held in
`payload->>'user_id'`, which is overloaded: a user uuid (the per-owner pool), `harness:<slug>`,
or `pot:<slug>`. `CanonicalVectorStore.search/list` post-filter each mem0 filter key against
`payload->>'<key>'`. The recall callers (`memory/injection.ts`, `agent-tools/memory/search.ts`)
fan out over `[user.id, harness:<slug>…, pot:<slug>…]` and merge.

The harness/pot pools are correctly scoped. **The `user.id` pool is recalled in EVERY
workspace** — so an owner's `project`-kind memories surface in all their workspaces (the
isolation leak). `payload.workspace_id` exists (remember.ts stamps `metadata.workspace_id =
ctx.principal.workspaceId`) but it was an attribution tag, never the recall axis. (The legacy
`workspace:`/`shared` SCOPE was deliberately deprecated + drained — do **not** revive it; that
would change the write-side scope-key model.)

## The fix (data-scoping-audit P-006 / D-004 / D-012)

**Structural — migration 398.** Promote the scope keys to first-class, indexed columns:
`memory_canonical.user_id` + `workspace_id` as `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'…') STORED`.
This auto-backfills every existing row, stays in lockstep with the payload the store already
writes (zero code change, behavior-neutral), and makes scope filterable/indexable without a
jsonb dig. (Same generated-mirror trick normalizes `workspace`→`workspace_id` on the telemetry
tables in mig 399.)

**Behavioral — `keepUserPoolHitForWorkspace` (workspace-scope-recall.ts).** A CONSERVATIVE,
NULL-safe post-filter on the **user pool only**, wired into both recall paths (injection.ts
filters `userResults`; search.ts filters hits where `scope === user.id`). Drop a hit **only**
when it explicitly carries a *different* `workspace_id` AND is not owner-tier:

- no / empty / non-string `workspace_id` (legacy, pre-stamping — the bulk of rows) → **keep**
- owner-tier `kind` ∈ `{user, feedback, reference}` (personal facts follow the owner) → **keep**
- no active workspace to compare → **keep** (fail-open)
- otherwise (a `project` hit tagged with another workspace) → **drop**

So flipping it never silently guts recall: only *new* cross-workspace `project` memories are
scoped out; harness/pot pools are untouched.

## The flag: graduated — defaults ON since the 2026-06-25 owner-attended flip

`FLAGS.MEMORY_WORKSPACE_SCOPED_RECALL` (`papercusp-memory-workspace-scoped-recall`) shipped as a
reversible **cutover** kill-switch, flipped after an **attended live recall-hit-rate verify** —
the owner watched the live A/B (the filter was already complete + unit-tested; recall is
emergent, so hit-rate was the thing to confirm, not a pre-gate). The flip landed 2026-06-25 and
the flag graduated OUT of `DARK_FLAGS` (`libs/flags/src/types.ts`) — it now **defaults ON**
(`FLAG_DEFAULTS['papercusp-memory-workspace-scoped-recall'] === true`). OFF remains available as
the reversible kill-switch if hit-rate ever regresses: sample real recall queries with the flag
ON vs OFF and confirm only cross-workspace `project` hits drop (owner-tier + same-ws +
legacy-NULL all still surface).

## Related: the wider `workspace_id DEFAULT 'default'` substrate is NOT this

29 coord_*/event_*/consolidated tables still carry `workspace_id text DEFAULT 'default'` with
live `'default'` data and no fill-trigger (P-007). Dropping those defaults is owner-gated
coord/presence SUBSTRATE work (writers must thread workspace_id first; the data must migrate off
`'default'`) — see `data-scoping-audit-2026-06-22` D-013. The `lint:no-workspace-default` guard
(`scripts/check-workspace-default-sql.mjs`) flags any NEW `workspace_id DEFAULT 'default'` so it
can't creep back while that attended migration is pending.
